diagnoses.rule_anchor: Test § 522(d)(5) independently for every property type, even when a specific exemption also applies or the asset exceeds that specific exemption's ceiling.
For each independently eligible citation, report the protected amount for the whole named asset.
Report the protected amount for the whole named asset as the lesser of its value and $300 for one debtor.
Include Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(p) independently for personal property, while retaining any applicable category-specific Oregon and federal citations.
Report the protected amount for the whole named asset as the lesser of its value and $400.
Test 735 Ill. Comp. Stat. 5/12-1001(b) as an independent alternative for any other personal property.
First apply the same category boundaries

examples.example: For a qualifying household item, the same asset's array can contain both § 522(d)(3) and § 522(d)(5); do not stop after the specific citation.
For a personally used prescribed health aid, the asset array contains both § 12-1001(e) and the independent § 12-1001(b) alternative.
A qualifying household item should retain both its category-specific Oregon citation and § 18.345(1)(p) in the same asset array.

Work-styled overalls remain wearing apparel when the facts do not state business use, so § 33-1125(1) receives the garment's value up to $500; an anniversary ring without an engagement-or-wedding fact receives no § 33-1125(4) claim.
Hypothetically, a $900 qualifying appliance with enough unused wildcard capacity receives separate alternatives of $700 under § 522(d)(3) and $900 under § 522(d)(5).

Hypothetically, a jointly owned high-value vehicle of two debtor spouses has separate asset-level alternatives of $8,000 under § 12-1001(b) and $2,400 under § 12-1001(c); do not double the motor-vehicle ceiling.
Hypothetically, a $24 household item has separate $24 alternatives under its household-goods provision and § 18.345(1)(p); the latter is not reported as $400 when the asset is worth less.

Hypothetically, a jointly owned $450 non-apparel item of two debtor spouses has a $450 § 8123 alternative, not $300 or $600; do not add the wearing-apparel provision merely because § 8123 also applies.
